body: AHAH :) ES6 ftw
What about we export the components pure and compose all the features in the widgets?
I see what you mean but cannot see a solution to do it from the widget/refinement-list.js for example. Do you know how?
Ok fixed
See https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/130/files#diff-4f0b4a4df70646a88f1c70e62161f72cR81
Why not defining that method as a function so you could avoid relying on `this`?
I would change the name of Pagination to make more explicit the composed aspect of this new Pagination component. Same goes for any component using this technique in the widgets.
Do you mean to avoid the .bind(null)?
Do you mean smg like `PaginationAutoHide` and then `RefinementListHeaderFooterAutoHide`?
ah yes, not using this here

When you execute the code as you did, the function that is passed to `toggleRefinements` prop is generic. The implementation I propose returns a function that is specific to the value of isRefined. This is more precise and does not rely on the value isRefined after it is generated nor depends on indirection.

Well I still have to pass every prop that is coming from the searchbox() call so it would be a function declaration inside the searchBox() but not defined in the object. Not sure it would be easier to grasp/reason about.

Even for others widgets I think we should not be affraid of adding _toggleRefine if it's a way for us to avoid creating function outside the widget() scope and passing a lot of parameters that were in the previous scope.

Yes I was thinking about defining inside the searchBox function so we can benefit from the closure.

My main argument was not readability but making this function not dependant on `this`. But this is not really a big deal in our case, because we are the users of those function (via instantSearch.js). I'm fine with leaving it in the object :)
Yes something like that :+1:
In the current implementation, the if check is done when toggleRefinement is done, not when the function is created. IMHO it's just best practice than real need here, your call.

Mixed feelings, on one hand this is very descriptive, on another hand this is a lot of letters for a variable name. And I fear we end up with `RefinementListHeaderFooterAutoHideAndSomeOtherBehaviorsThatWeWillHate`.

As for determining what are the behaviors of `<Pagination>` right now you just have to the top and see what are the decorators, should not be something we need to deal with a lot of times.
Autocompletion? :) But ok :)
